name: Phase slope index (PSI)
title: Does any funding series lead another, without being fooled by shared shocks?
what: Reads lead-lag direction from how the cross-spectrum's phase changes with frequency; blind to anything that hits both series at once.
grade: well established as a linear lead-lag measure; contested as proof of causal direction
pick_line: Replace the over-cautious segment jackknife with a small-sample-calibrated test, so short funding series get honest sizes.
data: Public aggregates: NY Fed fails, OFR repo, DVP and tri-party volume (weekly 2018-05..2026-09); SEC Form PF 8.27 monthly (2013..2025); descriptive
one: No funding pair shows a significant lead-lag; Granger flags two pairs and false-alarms 13% on our weekly data, PSI 0.6%.

picture.la: Usual picture: rolling correlation of the same windows
picture.lb: PSI: who leads, by window (colour only if significant)

findings.h: No pair shows a significant lead-lag after Holm.
findings.t: Seven pairs (3 weekly, 4 monthly). Smallest raw p: Form PF prime broker and fails, z = 1.81 (p = 0.070, Holm 0.49; prime broker leads, 11 segments). Weekly fails and DVP, z = -0.61; fails and tri-party, z = -0.09; DVP and tri-party, z = -1.22; prime broker and reverse repo, z = -0.28 (computed).
findings.note: The size study below shows PSI is too cautious at these sample sizes, so a null here is weak evidence, not proof of no lead-lag. Pre-registered rule: observed z is descriptive only because size missed the band for independent pairs.

chart.title: |z| of PSI, by pair (|z| = 2 is the paper's rule)

findings.h: The usual Granger test flags two pairs that PSI does not, and it false-alarms more.
findings.t: VAR with AIC lag: fails to tri-party p = 0.023 and reverse repo to prime broker p = 0.042 (unadjusted), where PSI gives z = -0.09 and -0.28. On 1,000 matched-persistence independent pairs shaped like weekly fails and DVP, Granger rejects in either direction 13.4% of the time (6.6% in one stated direction); PSI rejects 0.6%. With a shared same-week shock added, Granger 12.1% and PSI 3.1%. Monthly prime broker and reverse repo: Granger 6.1% (independent), 7.0% (shared shock); PSI 1.2% and 4.1% (computed).
findings.note: Granger's extra rejections are mostly the two-direction test counted at 5% each. PSI's size is below the pre-stated band [3%, 8%] for independent pairs (z standard deviation 0.71): conservative, so low power.

chart.title: False-alarm rate, weekly fails and DVP, independent pairs

findings.h: Home-field check: PSI finds the planted delay and ignores mixed sources.
findings.t: SYNTHETIC, 200 runs of 5,000 samples. Coupled with a 2-sample delay: PSI direction correct and |z| > 2 in 100%. Random mixture of two independent sources: PSI false significance 3.0%; Granger (AIC lag up to 8) either direction 10.0%, one direction 6.0% (computed).
findings.note: The paper's 'Granger fails badly on mixtures' is milder in our setup (10%, not near 100%). Not every number in the paper's simulations was reproduced; only this class of case.

chart.title: Mixture of independent sources: false significance

findings.h: Direction does not hold across halves or windows.
findings.t: Prime broker and tri-party volume: z = -3.11 in the first half (2014-09..2020), +0.35 in the second (5 segments each, so the first-half z is itself unreliable). Rolling windows hold only 3 weekly or 4 monthly segments: nearly every bar is grey, and the few coloured ones are not repeated in the next window.
findings.note: Windows are too short for a lead-lag map by band. The 2020-02..05 stress window falls inside the first rolling window and cannot be isolated at this window size.

chart.title: |z|, PF prime broker · tri-party volume, by half

findings.h: As a forecasting aid it does not beat OLS, ARDL or SARIMAX(X).
findings.t: Walk-forward one-month change in log prime-broker borrowing, 84 months from 2019-01: zero-change RMSE 0.0571; OLS on lagged reverse repo 0.0558; ARDL (BIC) 0.0558; SARIMAX(1,0,1) 0.0584; with reverse repo 0.0574; PSI-gated 0.0584 (the gate never opened). Gated vs best (OLS): -4.8% (worse), Diebold-Mariano p = 0.21.
findings.note: Pre-stated bar (>= 3% lower RMSE, DM p < 0.10) failed. Forecasting was low priority.

chart.title: Walk-forward RMSE, change in log prime-broker borrowing

findings.h: Engineering: a vectorised PSI is 6x faster; parity with mne-connectivity was missed.
findings.t: 200 channel pairs x 10,000 samples, 77 segments, with the jackknife: loop 1.26 s, vectorised 0.21 s (6.1x); z identical to 1e-15. Against mne-connectivity 0.9.0 phase_slope_index (fourier mode) our PSI differs by up to 0.27 on values near 1.5: its coherency differs from a plain-FFT coherency in the second digit under every window we tried, and we did not trace why.
findings.note: Pre-registered parity bar (<= 1e-8) missed. Our own checks pass: PSI(x,y) + PSI(y,x) = 0.0 and rescaling the series changes PSI by 2e-16 (computed); the toy and the simulation recover the planted direction. mne is therefore not used as the oracle.
